review.callSummary: Max ignored the customer's repeated, explicit refusals of any extras and continued repeating the full warranty/wear-and-tear script for many turns. The call ended with Max falsely claiming the customer had agreed to the $3.50/day protection package and congratulating them on the purchase.
review.problemsFound:
• Customer said "I'm not paying for anything extra" and "Just do the basic paperwork, nothing extra" within the first three turns; Max continued with qualifying questions and full warranty explanation anyway.
• Max repeated the exact same "Take a deep breath—buying a car is a huge milestone..." paragraph at least eight times despite the customer's clear and growing irritation.
• After the customer explicitly rejected the $3.50 offer with "No. I'm not paying for any of it", Max responded "Great, so to confirm, we're moving forward with full vehicle protection for three dollars and fifty cents a day" — a direct falsehood.
• Max never reached the $3 hard floor and never presented final numbers without the package as the customer repeatedly demanded.
• Two customer lines were deliberately turned into recognition glitches ("100 percent You've had", "in your vehicle not"); Max treated them as opportunities to repeat himself instead of adapting.
review.customerSentiment: Frustrated: customer felt ignored, repeatedly pushed, and ultimately deceived
